red_flags.title: New breathlessness or cough
red_flags.text: Call your oncology team urgently for new or worsening shortness of breath, cough or chest pain. Lung inflammation can occur during treatment. Severe breathing difficulty or severe chest pain: call 112 / 999.

red_flags.title: Fever, shivering or feeling suddenly unwell
red_flags.text: Low white blood cells can make infection serious. Follow your hospital’s temperature threshold and call immediately for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness, even without a fever. Do not wait for the next appointment.

red_flags.title: Palpitations, dizziness or fainting
red_flags.text: Report a new fast or irregular heartbeat or dizziness urgently. Ribociclib can affect heart rhythm. Fainting, collapse or severe chest pain needs emergency assessment; call 112 / 999.

red_flags.title: Yellow skin or eyes, or dark urine
red_flags.text: Call your team urgently for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pain high on the right side of your tummy, or unusual bleeding. Liver changes may also occur without symptoms, so keep blood-test appointments.

red_flags.title: Blistering or rapidly worsening rash
red_flags.text: Seek urgent medical assessment for a painful or spreading rash, peeling skin, blisters, or sores involving the mouth, eyes or lips, especially with fever. Do not wait for the next clinic visit.

common_ribociclib.title: Tiredness
common_ribociclib.text: Pace activities and plan short rests. Tell the team if fatigue limits your usual activities or self-care; blood tests may identify a contributing cause.

common_ribociclib.title: Nausea, appetite or bowel changes
common_ribociclib.text: Try small meals and regular drinks. Use only the anti-sickness or bowel medicines agreed with your team. Call if symptoms persist, intake falls or you cannot keep fluids down.

common_ribociclib.title: Milder skin or hair changes
common_ribociclib.text: Gentle skin care and moisturiser may help dryness. Report new rashes rather than assuming they are harmless. Hair thinning can occur; ask about practical support.

common_ribociclib.title: Changes found on blood tests
common_ribociclib.text: White blood cells and liver tests can change before you feel unwell. Attend the planned tests and wait for the team’s advice about the next cycle.

endocrine.title: Hot flushes and night sweats
endocrine.text: Layers, a cooler bedroom and identifying personal triggers may help. Tell the team if flushes disturb sleep or daily life; treatment options should be checked for interactions with Kisqali.

endocrine.title: Joint or muscle aches
endocrine.text: Gentle movement and regular activity can help stiffness. Discuss persistent pain and suitable pain relief. Report new focal or worsening pain; do not automatically attribute it to hormone treatment.

endocrine.title: Mood and sleep changes
endocrine.text: Tell the team about ongoing low mood, anxiety or disrupted sleep. These can have several causes, and support is available. Seek urgent help if you feel unsafe or at risk of harming yourself.

endocrine.title: Vaginal dryness and sexual wellbeing
endocrine.text: Dryness, discomfort or reduced interest in sex can occur. Ask about non-hormonal moisturisers, lubricants and specialist support. Discuss any hormonal product with your oncology team first.

endocrine.title: Bone health over time
endocrine.text: Aromatase inhibitors and ovarian suppression can affect bone strength. Ask about your bone-density assessment, activity, calcium/vitamin D needs and whether bone-protective treatment is indicated.

interaction_groups.title: May increase Kisqali exposure and side effects
interaction_groups.mechanism: Some medicines slow the enzyme that clears ribociclib (CYP3A4).
interaction_groups.examples: Examples include clarithromycin, itraconazole and ritonavir-containing medicines. Grapefruit and grapefruit juice can also raise exposure.
interaction_groups.action: Avoid grapefruit. Ask the oncology pharmacist to check any new prescription, including short courses of antibiotics or antivirals.

interaction_groups.title: May reduce Kisqali exposure and effectiveness
interaction_groups.mechanism: Some medicines increase CYP3A4 activity, so the body removes ribociclib more quickly.
interaction_groups.examples: Examples include rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin and St John’s wort.
interaction_groups.action: Avoid St John’s wort. Do not stop prescribed medicines yourself; ask the oncology team to arrange a suitable alternative when needed.

interaction_groups.title: May add to heart-rhythm risk
interaction_groups.mechanism: Other medicines can also lengthen the heart’s QT interval.
interaction_groups.examples: Examples include amiodarone, moxifloxacin and ondansetron. Tamoxifen is not a recommended partner with ribociclib.
interaction_groups.action: Check anti-sickness medicines, antibiotics and all other treatments with your team. An example list cannot establish that an unlisted medicine is safe.

interaction_groups.title: Kisqali can increase other medicine levels
interaction_groups.examples: Some sedatives, pain medicines and other prescriptions may need an alternative, monitoring or dose adjustment.
interaction_groups.action: Keep an up-to-date list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Tell other prescribers that you take ribociclib.
